Checks the ISO 13616 structure and mod-97 checksum. It cannot verify that the account exists.

📖 How to use

  1. Paste or type the IBAN (spaces are fine).
  2. The format is checked, then the official mod-97 checksum runs.
  3. A green result means the IBAN is structurally valid.
  4. Use the grouped format and country code for copying into bank forms.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How does IBAN validation work?

The first four characters are moved to the end, every letter is replaced by two digits (A=10 … Z=35), and the resulting number must leave remainder 1 when divided by 97.

Does a valid IBAN mean the account exists?

No. A valid checksum only proves the IBAN is well-formed. It cannot confirm the account exists, is open, or belongs to anyone.

Is my IBAN sent to a server?

No — validation runs entirely in your browser and the IBAN is never stored or sent anywhere.
